QuestionText: Which of these is excluded from the movement area?
Option2: Grass areas specified for aircraft use
ExplanationText: The movement area is the manoeuvring area, the aprons and any part provided for aircraft maintenance. Buildings are not part of it.

QuestionText: Which area excludes the apron and any part used for aircraft maintenance?
ExplanationText: Take the apron and the maintenance areas out of the movement area and what is left is the manoeuvring area.

QuestionText: Where is the pre-flight altimeter check made, and what is the maximum difference from the average elevation?
Option1: On the apron, 3 m or 10 ft
ExplanationText: It belongs on the apron so it can be done before taxi clearance. No part may be more than 3 m, or 10 ft, from the average elevation.

QuestionText: What is the runway width for a code 4E runway?
ExplanationText: Code 4 gives 45 m for C, D and E. Only code 4F needs 60 m.

QuestionText: For a code 4 precision approach runway, how far must the strip extend beyond the runway end, and how far each side of the centreline?
ExplanationText: At least 60 m beyond the end for code 2, 3 and 4, and 150 m each side of the centreline for a code 3 or 4 precision or non-precision runway.

QuestionText: What is the minimum RESA length from the end of the strip, and the recommended length for a code 3 or 4 runway?
ExplanationText: Not less than 90 m is the standard. 240 m is the recommendation for code 3 and 4, and 120 m for code 1 and 2.

QuestionText: A clearway is added at the end of the runway. Which declared distance changes?
ExplanationText: A clearway is not pavement, so only TODA grows, and it is capped at 1.5 times TORA.

QuestionText: A stopway is added at the end of the runway. Which declared distance changes?
ExplanationText: A stopway is pavement but only for stopping, so only ASDA grows.

QuestionText: The threshold is displaced 300 m down the runway. Which declared distance changes?
ExplanationText: Only LDA. The pavement before the new threshold can still be used for take-off.

QuestionText: What is the required intersecting angle for a rapid exit taxiway, and the design turn-off speed in the wet on a code 4 runway?
Option0: 25 to 45 degrees, preferably 30. 93 km/h or 50 kt
Option1: 30 to 60 degrees, preferably 45. 65 km/h or 35 kt
Option3: 25 to 45 degrees, preferably 30. 65 km/h or 35 kt
ExplanationText: Not more than 45 degrees, not less than 25, preferably 30. The design speed in the wet is 93 km/h, which is 50 kt, on code 3 and 4 runways.

QuestionText: How far from the runway centreline is the holding position for a precision CAT II runway, code 4?
ExplanationText: 90 m for precision CAT I, II and III on code 3 and 4 runways. For code F that figure becomes 107.5 m.

QuestionText: What is the only type of fixed object normally permitted inside a runway strip?
Option1: Visual aids such as PAPIs, and they must be frangible
ExplanationText: Visual aids are the exception, and they must be frangible. Everything else inside the stated dimensions is an obstacle.
